title: This 'Dead' Star Fooled Astronomers for 15 Years 🤯

scenes.narration: For fifteen years, this star fooled astronomers into thinking it had exploded.
scenes.headline: The star that faked its death

visual.ai_prompt: a massive star exploding in deep space, bright shock wave, glowing debris

scenes.narration: In 2012, telescopes spotted what looked like a supernova, a star blowing itself apart, in a galaxy about 25 million light-years away.
scenes.headline: A 'supernova' in 2012

visual.ai_prompt: a vast spiral galaxy seen from far away, billions of stars

scenes.narration: But it kept doing something exploded stars don't do. It brightened, faded, and brightened again.
scenes.headline: It kept coming back

visual.ai_prompt: a giant blue star flaring and dimming, surrounded by glowing gas

scenes.narration: Now NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory has caught it mid-outburst, and found a hidden partner: a black hole or a neutron star.
scenes.headline: A hidden partner

visual.ai_prompt: an X-ray space telescope orbiting Earth, sunlight on its panels

scenes.narration: It circles the star about every 113 days, feeding on it, and heating gas the star threw off years ago.
scenes.headline: A cosmic feast

visual.ai_prompt: a black hole pulling gas from a nearby blue star into a glowing disk

scenes.narration: That glowing gas creates the illusion of an explosion. The star never died. Something is feeding on it. Follow for more stories like this.
scenes.headline: Not dead, just dinner

visual.ai_prompt: a glowing cloud of gas lit from inside, pink and teal colours

description: A star in galaxy NGC 4559 looked like a supernova in 2012, but kept brightening and fading. NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory shows a hidden black hole or neutron star is feeding on it.
